about.seoDescription: An overview of PSRay: how PSN data is collected and updated, how to request removal or hiding, the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, who runs the site, documentation and frequently asked questions.
about.title: Play. Collect. Look back.
about.lead: PSRay is a community service for finding and organizing PlayStation trophy data and sharing tips with other players. This page explains how the data shown here is handled and how the site is run.

intro.title: About PSRay
intro.mission: PSRay brings profiles, earned trophies, recently played games and leaderboards together in an easy-to-read form, and aims to be a place where players share tips for every trophy.
intro.ai: PSRay is built with the help of AI tools such as Claude and GPT.
intro.disclaimer: PSRay is an independent service run by an individual. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or officially connected to Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc., PlayStation or any of their affiliates. PlayStation and related names and trademarks belong to their respective owners.

policies.lead: The conditions for using PSRay with peace of mind, and how your data is handled.

terms.body: Rules for accounts, posts, prohibited conduct and use of the service.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.body: How personal data, public PSN information, cookies and removal requests are handled.

data.title: About the data we show

collection.title: How data is collected
collection.body: PSRay collects the player profiles, games, trophies and trophy progress that are publicly visible on PlayStation Network. It also shows content users post to PSRay directly, such as tips.

updates.title: How data is updated
updates.body: PSRay’s data is updated by reading information from PSN. Depending on when PSN reflects changes, what you see here may lag behind.

data.notice: Changing your PSN privacy settings doesn’t necessarily update or remove information PSRay has already stored right away. If you don’t want to be listed, use the hiding request below.

removal.title: Removing or hiding data
removal.lead: Hiding public PSN data and deleting an account you registered on PSRay are separate procedures.

request.title: Send a request
request.body: Email us the PSN ID concerned and which procedure you’d like.

verify.title: Verify ownership
verify.body: We confirm you own the account in a safe way, for example by asking you to add a temporary code to your PSN About Me.

hide.title: Hide the profile
hide.body: Once verified, we stop showing it publicly and prevent normal syncs from adding it again.

password.title: Never send us your PSN password
password.body: The PSRay team will never ask for your PSN password, verification codes or security questions.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.body: PSRay is still under active development, and some features will be rolled out over time. Maintenance and feature updates are announced on the operator’s Twitter (X) account.

bugs.title: Bugs & data corrections
bugs.body: To report a bug or incorrect data, include the page URL, the PSN ID and details. Please send reports to the operator’s Twitter (X) account.

markdown.body: Formatting, images, spoilers and extended blocks you can use in tips.

api.body: Endpoints and samples for reading trophy sets, profiles, games and series, with a console to try them.

official.question: Is PSRay an official PlayStation service?
official.answer: No. PSRay is an independently run community service. It is not endorsed by, affiliated with or operated by Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. or its affiliates.

account.question: Do I need an account to use PSRay?
account.answer: No. You don’t need a PSRay account to view public profiles, trophy data, leaderboards or tips. Posting tips and some community features require signing up.

notFound.question: I searched for a player but can’t find them.
notFound.answer: They may not have been synced to PSRay yet, or their PSN privacy settings may prevent us from reading their data. Check the spelling of the PSN ID, then try updating from the sync page.

outdated.question: Trophies or profile details aren’t up to date.
outdated.answer: PSRay’s data isn’t real-time. Sync processing, caching and the time PSN takes to reflect changes can all cause delays. Please wait a while, then sync again.

private.question: Will information I made private on PSN still be shown?
private.answer: PSRay may keep information that was public when it was collected. Changing your privacy settings may not immediately affect data that’s already stored. If you want it removed, please use the data hiding request.

relisting.question: Can a profile be listed again after it’s removed?
relisting.answer: For hiding requests where ownership has been verified, we hide the existing public profile and make sure normal sync actions don’t make the same account public again.

report.question: Where can I report incorrect data or bugs?
report.answer: Email us with the PSN ID, the URL of the page concerned, a description of the problem and, if possible, the steps to reproduce it. Please don’t send confidential information or passwords.

tips.question: Can anyone post trophy tips?
tips.answer: Users who have registered on PSRay and meet the required conditions can post. Posts are subject to the Terms of Service and community rules. See the guide for details on writing Markdown.

api.question: Is there a PSRay API?
api.answer: Yes. The public endpoints for trophy sets, player profiles, games and series need no API key; see the API documentation for how to use them. Please cache results and avoid frequent requests.

apiDocs.seoDescription: How to use the public PSRay API: endpoints, parameters, response fields and samples for trophy sets, player profiles, games and series, with a console to try each request.
apiDocs.lead: Read PSRay's trophy sets, player profiles, games and series with plain HTTP requests. This page covers the most common public, read-only endpoints, and you can try each one right here.

points.noPrefix: Paths follow the base URL directly; there is no {prefix} prefix.
points.noAuth: Every endpoint on this page is a GET request that needs neither a login nor an API key.
points.cors: Cross-origin requests are allowed from any origin, so you can call the API straight from a browser.

responses.success: On success the result is in {data}. List endpoints also return {meta} with the page number, page size, total count and total pages. Asking for a page past the end returns an empty array, not an error.
responses.failure: On failure you get the matching HTTP status and an {error} object. {code} is a stable error code, so branch on it in your code. {message} is an English description, and when parameter validation fails, {details} gives the reason for each field.
responses.requestId: Every response carries an {header} header, and error responses repeat it as {field}. Include it when you report a problem so we can find the request in our logs.
responses.time: Timestamps are ISO 8601 strings in UTC, for example {example}.

languages.body: Trophy set titles, trophy names, game names and series names come in several languages. The API picks the display language in this order:

steps.header: The {header} request header, highest weight first
steps.fallback: If neither is given or nothing matches, the item's default language

languages.normalize: Chinese is mapped to PSN's language variants by region: {tw} is treated as {hant}, and {cn} as {hans}.
languages.field: {field} in the response tells you which language was used. {name} is always the original title; show {localized} in your interface.

errors.body: All errors share one format, so you can tell them apart by {code}. These are the codes the endpoints on this page can return.

codes.notFound: The path does not exist, or an ID is not a number
codes.trophySetNotFound: The trophy set does not exist
codes.userNotFound: PSRay has no such player (never synced, or the account was deleted)
codes.userBanned: The player has been permanently suspended
codes.seriesNotFound: The series does not exist or is not published yet
codes.methodNotAllowed: Wrong request method; the endpoints on this page accept GET only
codes.internal: Internal server error; please try again later

items.cache: Please cache results and avoid frequent polling or bulk scraping. There is no rate limit today, but abusive sources may be blocked.
items.fields: Responses may gain new fields over time, so ignore the ones you don't recognise. Fields not listed on this page may change; don't rely on them.
items.data: The data is PSN's public trophy information, synced by PSRay at intervals, so it can lag behind. Players who set their profile to private don't have their trophy data published.
items.feedback: Found a problem or have a suggestion? Let us know on the {link} board.

usage.stability: The API is still evolving; changes will be reflected on this page.

endpoint.fieldsNote: Only the most-used fields are listed; see the sample response for the full shape.

trophiesBrowse.title: Browse trophy sets
trophiesBrowse.description: Lists trophy sets page by page. Search by title, filter by platform or by whether there is a platinum, and sort by newest, trending or most players.

trophiesShow.title: Trophy set details
trophiesShow.description: Returns everything about one trophy set: its groups and all trophies, available languages, recent players, and the game and series it belongs to. Pass psnid to add that player's public progress.

profileShow.title: Player profile
profileShow.description: Returns a player's profile: trophy level, trophy counts by type, rankings, a trophy calendar for the past year and their latest comments. Private profiles still return 200, with is_profile_public set to false and calendar set to null.

gamesBrowse.title: Browse games
gamesBrowse.description: Lists games page by page, newest first release first. Search by name or alias and filter by platform.

gamesShow.title: Game details
gamesShow.description: Returns a game's summary, aliases, release dates per platform and region, external links, and its trophy sets and series.

seriesBrowse.title: Browse series
seriesBrowse.description: Lists game series page by page. Search by series name or the titles of its games, and sort by popularity, latest release or name.

seriesShow.title: Series details
seriesShow.description: Returns the series' games in order, main entries and spin-offs alike, each with its trophy sets. Pass psnid to add that player's progress through the series.

params.lang: Display language, for example zh-Hans, ja or en; see Display language
params.langTips: Display language for trophy and trophy set names in the latest comments
params.qTrophies: Search terms, matched against the original title, every official localized title and the NPWR ID; a bare number or #number matches the ID exactly. Results are sorted by relevance and sort is ignored
params.qGames: Search terms, matched against the name, localized names and aliases (such as FF7R)
params.qSeries: Search terms, matched against the series name and the titles of its trophy sets
params.sortTrophies: Order: newest by date added, trending by players in the last 7 days, popular by total players
params.sortSeries: Order: popular by popularity, recent by latest release year, name by name
params.platformGames: Filter by platform; accepts several, for example PS5, PS4, PC, SWITCH
params.hasPlatinum: true returns only trophy sets with a platinum, false only those without
params.trophySetId: Trophy set ID (PSRay's numeric ID, not the NPWR ID)
params.psnidPath: The player's PSN Online ID, case-insensitive
params.psnidProgress: Adds this player's progress on the trophy set (public profiles only)
params.psnidSeries: Adds this player's progress through the series (public profiles only)

fields.names: Original title, and the title picked for the display language (show the latter)
fields.npwr: PSN trophy set ID, for example NPWR11556_00
fields.definedTrophies: Trophy count per type: bronze, silver, gold, platinum
fields.rates: Platinum and completion rates in percent; may be null
fields.medianTime: Median time to complete, in seconds
fields.trophySet: The trophy set itself, with much the same fields as a list item
fields.displayLanguage: The display language used for this response
fields.availableLanguages: Available languages and their titles, unofficial translations included
fields.groups: Trophy groups: the base game and each add-on
fields.trophies: Trophies in the group: type, name, description, icon, earn rate and rarity
fields.recentPlayers: Public players who earned trophies most recently, up to 10
fields.game: The game, shaped like a game list item; null when not linked
fields.viewerProgress: Progress of the player given as psnid; null when not found or private
fields.country: Country or region code, for example JP
fields.level: Trophy level, and progress to the next level (0 to 100)
fields.rank: Global and regional rank; null when not ranked
fields.calendar: Trophies earned per day over the past year, each with date and count; null when private or the showcase is off
fields.recentTips: The 5 latest comments; null for players who haven’t signed up on PSRay or when the showcase is off
fields.showcases: Showcases to render: left and right list keys (calendar, rarest, featured, games, text_left, tips, social, text_right) in the owner’s order, only those switched on and with content
fields.rarestTrophies: The 6 earned trophies with the lowest PSN rate, each with its trophy and set; null when private or the showcase is off
fields.featuredTrophies: Trophies the owner picked (up to 12, in their order); null when private or the showcase is off
fields.favoriteGames: Played games (trophy sets) the owner picked, up to 6 in their order; null when private or the showcase is off
fields.texts: The left and right column texts, each with title and body (Markdown); null when the showcase is off or the body is empty. Returned for private profiles too
fields.accounts: Accounts on other platforms, in the owner's order, each with platform, value and url (null for the friend code and gamertag, which have no link); null when the showcase is off or empty. Returned for private profiles too
fields.cover: Cover image with URL, size and main colour; may be null
fields.releaseDate: First release date; null when not yet announced
fields.platforms: Platforms it was released on, each with code, name and abbreviation
fields.summary: Summary, and the summary picked for the display language
fields.aliases: Aliases, such as abbreviations or former titles
fields.releases: Release dates per platform and region
fields.links: Pages on external databases such as IGDB
fields.trophySets: Linked trophy sets, shaped like Browse trophy sets items
fields.covers: Up to 4 icons of key entries, for building a cover
fields.stageCounts: Number of main entries and spin-offs
fields.seriesTrophySetCount: Total number of trophy sets in the series
fields.popularity: Popularity: the sum of players across the main entries
fields.years: Release years of the first and latest main entries
fields.tierTotals: Trophy totals per type across the main entries (the most-played version of each)
fields.stages: Entries in order; kind is main or side
fields.entries: Trophy sets for the entry, such as versions for different platforms
fields.viewer: Progress through the series of the player given as psnid; null when psnid is omitted

screenshots.title: Screenshots
screenshots.description: Upload and manage your game screenshots. Public ones appear in the showcases on your profile.
screenshots.emptyHint: Drop pictures on the upload card, or click it to pick several at once.
screenshots.deleteBody: Delete this screenshot? The picture is deleted right away and can't be restored.

upload.formats: JPEG, PNG or WebP, several at once. Anything over 2560 px on the long side is scaled down; all are stored as WebP
upload.watermarkProfileHint: Logo and your profile link in the bottom right
upload.watermarkFinal: Watermarks are drawn into the picture and can't be changed after uploading.
